Subject: SIG: Control plane dependency catalogue request

Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of Veridian's SIG/CAIQ intake for our upcoming audit, we need a concise inventory of Redwood's control plane dependencies for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically we are looking for:

- A CSV (or similar) enumerating control-plane components (service names), their function, hosting boundary (hosted/dedicated/private), and whether any 3rd-party services are required at runtime (e.g., KMS, external DNS, SaaS telemetry).
- An annotated topology diagram that highlights which network paths are control-plane only versus data-plane, and where tenant isolation is enforced (edge, VPC peering, sidecar, etc.).
- Short notes on any shared control-plane services that span customer instances and how authentication/authorization is enforced.

Can you deliver the CSV + diagram by EOD PDT? If not, please propose a short timeline. If helpful, I'm happy to accept a first-pass CSV and a diagram that we can iterate on with your security/architecture team.

Appreciate it — Devon

Hi Devon / Ben / Tessa,

Thanks — attaching the annotated topology and boundary narrative. Quick clarifications to help the SIG mapping:

Attachments included: topology-annotated.png, private-dedicated-boundary.pdf

Short notes (high level):
- Control plane components: orchestration API (control-plane-api), scheduler, model registry meta-service, control-plane-auth (OAuth2/JWKS), telemetry-collector (internal), and orchestration-catalog (service metadata). These are all deployed in our control plane layer; in Hosted mode they run in Redwood-managed cloud accounts; in Dedicated they run in a dedicated cluster fenced by network ACLs and tenant VPC peering; in Private they run in a customer-managed control plane (when requested) or in a private VPC with our control plane agents.
- Shared services: KMS (customer-managed for Private; Redwood-managed for Hosted), central audit-log aggregator (we offer retention controls per contract), and metrics ingestion (SaaS) — note: metrics ingestion can be routed to customer endpoints for Private installs.
- Network demarcation: control-plane traffic is restricted to management subnets; data-plane inference requests route to tenant GPU pools and are subject to separate egress rules. The topology highlights the demarcation at the edge router and at the sidecar boundary.
- AuthZ: all control-plane APIs validate tokens issued by our control-plane auth service; Private deployments can be configured to use customer identity providers via OIDC federation (documented in the PDF).

Open items we will complete for the SIG CSV: service versions, public/private hosting column, whether the dependency is 1st party or 3rd party, and the required network ports for firewall mapping. Expect the polished CSV and a Drive link from Rishi shortly.

-Kim
